meta.title: Check your understanding: The Solar Odyssey timeline

objectives: Describe how the photovoltaic effect was found in a solid and then explained by Einstein's photons
Explain why space was the first real market for solar cells
Estimate how many times cheaper a watt of solar module became between 1975 and 2024

questions.prompt: In 1873 Willoughby Smith saw the resistance of selenium drop in light. In 1877 Adams and Day got a current from lit selenium. Why does only the 1877 experiment count as the photovoltaic effect in a solid?
choices: Adams and Day used sunlight, while Smith used lamplight
Current flowed with no battery in the circuit; Smith's selenium still needed one
Smith's selenium was dissolved in a liquid, so it was not a solid
Adams and Day measured electrons flying off the selenium surface
questions.explain: Smith saw photoconductivity: light freed extra charge carriers, but a battery still had to drive the current. Adams and Day's selenium made the current by itself, which is the photovoltaic effect. Electrons flying off a surface would be the photoelectric effect, a different thing.

questions.prompt: Einstein's 1905 idea explained why dim ultraviolet light frees electrons from a metal while bright red light does not. What was the key point?
choices: Brighter light makes each photon carry more energy
Red light is absorbed by the air before it reaches the metal
Ultraviolet light always carries more total power than red light
Each photon's energy depends only on its colour, and red photons are each too small
questions.explain: Light comes in packets, and a single packet must carry enough energy on its own. Brightness only changes how many packets arrive, not how big each one is, so no amount of red light does what one ultraviolet photon can.

questions.prompt: Why was space, rather than homes or power stations, the first real market for solar cells after 1954?
choices: In orbit, cost mattered less than weight and reliability
Early cells only worked in the cold of space
Solar power stations were not allowed until the oil shock
Satellites needed far more power than a home
questions.explain: Early cells were far too expensive for ordinary uses, but a satellite needs light, long-lasting power and can pay for it. Vanguard 1's solar-powered transmitter ran for more than six years, long after its battery-powered one had gone silent.

questions.prompt: In constant dollars a solar module cost about $132 per watt in 1975 and about $0.27 per watt in 2024. Roughly how many times cheaper did it become?
choices: About 100 times, since the price fell by 99.8 %
questions.explain: Divide the old price by the new one: 132 ÷ 0.27 ≈ 490, roughly 500 times. A 99.8 % fall is not a factor of 100: what is left is 0.2 % of the old price, which is one five-hundredth.
